blocks.body:
## Executive Summary

- **Local Safeguard 6 acceptance passes.** The matrix retains all 5,161 source instruments, contract identity has zero cross-asset collisions, and every profiled default public endpoint stays within the byte and local latency ceilings.
- **The identity boundary is materially safer.** Fifty-five raw mixed-class ids reconcile to zero canonical mixed ids; option is now a contract type rather than an underlying class; CAT and SPCX ambiguities remain source-scoped.
- **Coverage is not the same as verification.** Only 93 of 1,169 RWA.xyz assets are verified; 1,076 remain explicitly unverified candidates.
- **Production promotion remains blocked.** Hyperliquid and derivative catalog artifacts are stale, the daily feed is only at a reconciled baseline, and the 14-day, rights, benchmark, manipulation, independence, migration, and human gates remain open.

## Public defaults are bounded without deleting data

The largest initial collections ranged from 1.62 MB to 15.16 MB, and three nested builders took 7.5–18.5 seconds locally. Defaults now return deterministic first pages or compact summaries. Full counts remain available through totals, filters, exact identity resolution, and stable `limit`/`offset` traversal. Consumers that assumed the entire registry arrived in one default response must migrate to pagination.

## Identity and contract grains are explicit

All 3,438 RWA.xyz token listings are preserved across 3,435 normalized network/address contracts. Three repeated listings belong to the same source assets and remain non-blocking; any incomplete identity or contract assigned to multiple source assets blocks decision-grade acceptance. The cross-class repair also preserves all 1,855 option contracts while assigning their actual underlyings, including XAUT metal and BTC crypto. A synthetic collision test proves the blocker now fails when it should.

## Freshness remains fail-closed

The response assembly timestamp is no longer presented as source freshness. The RWA.xyz catalog snapshot is current within its declared cadence, while the Hyperliquid tradeable and derivative venue catalogs are stale. The daily agent reconciles to canonical SHA-256 `f07f4bed75a032c53ac226ebd0fda531cb2a31457bf0479d624dad13cc593a42` and correctly reports `baseline_created`; a second distinct verified snapshot is required before making a no-change or delta claim.

## Required Next Actions

1. Refresh the Hyperliquid and derivative catalog artifacts through their reviewed read-only capture paths, then rerun snapshot and cross-class reconciliation.
2. Capture a second distinct canonical RWA.xyz snapshot and prove daily delta/no-new behavior without silently reusing a baseline.
3. Migrate the production pilot history into schema v3 with zero rejected valid rows and reconcile exact counts before any release.
4. Continue the three-feed pilot until the full 14-day/672-sample window and every rights, benchmark, manipulation/depth, independence, and human approval gate pass.
5. Update every registry client and generated integration skill to follow pagination and exact-resolution links.

## Reproducibility and Caveats

The executed notebook is the canonical local evidence record and contains eight successful code cells with no error outputs. Endpoint timing was measured in one local cold-process run and should not be interpreted as a production latency SLO. The analysis used checked-in catalog snapshots without external refresh and made no production mutation, commit, push, deployment, or promotion. Unverified RWA.xyz mappings remain source-scoped candidates regardless of catalog coverage.
